kubernetes.description: The kubernetes manager matches no files until it is told which ones, and this repository keeps its manifests in two places

packageRules.description: Kubernetes libraries and the tools generating against them move as one release train: k8s.io/* is a set of staging repos cut from one tag, and controller-runtime, controller-tools and setup-envtest each track a specific one of those tags. Raising one without the others gives a tree that does not build. config:recommended already groups the k8s.io staging repos as `kubernetes monorepo`; joining the same group is what puts everything on one branch. The k8s.io/* members are named here as well rather than left to the preset, so that a rename upstream shows up as a group that does not exist instead of as a silent split

The images in the manifests are gated itself and the test scaffolding built from hack/. The scaffolding is tagged by the build that made it and exists in no registry, so looking is only a failed lookup. gated is published, but the tag written here names the branch rather than a version (ADR 0029): it is what a checkout runs, and it moves on its own. Where a version has to be chosen, an overlay writes it, and the repository holding that overlay is where Renovate belongs

The ACME test server and its DNS server are pulled by a tag that keeps moving, so a checkout does not say which image an end-to-end run used. Pinning the digest makes the Dockerfile the one place the version is stated, which is what the file was there for, and leaves Renovate to move it

Workflows are already read by the github-actions manager. Grouping them keeps a handful of actions from arriving as a handful of pull requests, since they are updated together and reviewed the same way
